lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: recognizing linear, quadratic, and exponential situations
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: recognizing linear, quadratic, and exponential situations

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: 500 grows 4% per year. Model and value after 3 years?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Quantity A grows by 24 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: A stays ahead permanently because 24 is larger than 3.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 1800(0.87)^t, with t in years. What does 0.87 represent?
choices: the value of the asset when it was new, $1800
the total value lost over the asset's life
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.87, meaning a 13% annual loss
the number of years until the asset is worthless

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (1, -10) and (5, -30). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 7, 13, 19, 25. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 6.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 6.

items.prompt: A population of 1200 grows by 10% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 3 years, to the nearest whole number.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: Quantity A grows by 97 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 3000(0.91)^t, with t in years. What does 0.91 represent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (1, -12) and (3, -26). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
